draft.title: Revolutionary parties
card: Three main revolutionary parties opposed the tsar. Each wanted to end autocracy, but they disagreed about who should lead change and how.
Bolsheviks
a Marxist party led by Lenin. They wanted a small, disciplined party of committed revolutionaries to lead the industrial workers.
Mensheviks
a Marxist party that wanted a larger, more open membership. They believed Russia must first pass through a middle-class stage of development before socialism.
Socialist Revolutionaries
a party that looked to the peasants, who were most of the population. They wanted land taken from large landowners and shared among peasants.
draft.remember: Bolsheviks: a tight party leading workers. Mensheviks: a broad party. SRs: peasants and land.

a.q: Which party mainly looked to the peasants and wanted land shared among them?
opts: Socialist Revolutionaries
Bolsheviks
Mensheviks
The Duma
a.why: The Socialist Revolutionaries built their appeal on the peasants, who were most of the population, and on land redistribution. The Bolsheviks were Marxists who looked to the industrial workers, so they are the tempting wrong choice.
a.clue: Which party's name does not point to Marxism?

b.q: At a meeting in 1903, one group argued for a small party of committed revolutionaries, and another for a larger, more open party. Which pairing is correct?
opts: Bolsheviks wanted the small party, Mensheviks the larger one
Mensheviks wanted the small party, Bolsheviks the larger one
Bolsheviks wanted the small party, SRs the larger one
SRs wanted the small party, Mensheviks the larger one
b.why: Lenin's Bolsheviks wanted a small, disciplined party to lead the workers, while the Mensheviks wanted a broader membership. The reversed pairing is tempting, but it swaps the two Marxist parties. The SRs were a separate party focused on the peasants.
b.clue: Which party did Lenin lead, and what did he want?

b.best: Bolsheviks wanted the small party, Mensheviks the larger one

problems.detail: The clue 'Which party's name does not point to Marxism?' is misleading. The names 'Bolshevik' and 'Menshevik' (majority and minority) do not point to Marxism either. 'Socialist Revolutionaries' is the one name that does suggest socialism, so the clue could steer students away from the right answer.

Bolsheviks

proposal.remember: Bolsheviks: a tight party leading workers. Mensheviks: a broad party. SRs: peasants and land.

a.q: In 1905 a peasant hoped his landlord's estate would be divided among his village. Which party's aims best matched his hopes?
opts: Socialist Revolutionaries
Bolsheviks
Mensheviks
The Duma
a.why: The Socialist Revolutionaries built their appeal on the peasants and on taking land from large landowners to share among them. The Bolsheviks are the tempting choice, but they were a Marxist party that looked to the industrial workers. The Duma was not a revolutionary party.
a.clue: Two of these parties grew out of one Marxist party.
